_doc: T-W8 HEADROOM + RETEST entry-candidate study -- FROZEN pre-registration (ground rule 12: exploratory != confirmatory; candidates + pass bar are frozen HERE, BEFORE the fresh-slice results are seen, so nothing gets re-picked after the fact). Do NOT edit candidates/thresholds/pass-bar after headroom-retest-tw8.json has been generated -- amend via a versioned amendment_log entry instead, same discipline as entry-exit-matrix-stop-a-preregistration.json.

hypothesis_provenance.narrative: The fleet's BULLISH_RECLAIM entry buys the FIRST break above a reclaimed level even when documented resistance sits directly overhead. On 2026-07-09 the engine entered at 09:43 ET with the 748.43 RTH-high + 748.78 memory-level (score 111, 63 touches) only $0.4-0.9 above the 747.5/747.93 reclaim; price rejected off 748.78, flushed, and 3 entries premium-stopped before the real break paid 70 minutes later.
hypothesis_provenance.why_excluded: 2026-07-09 generated this hypothesis -- including it in either window would let the study confirm itself on the very day it was mined from. Exploratory window ends 2026-06-18; fresh window ends 2026-07-08. Neither reaches 2026-07-09.

exploratory.hash_convention: sha256 of the raw file bytes
exploratory.status: BURNED -- prior T3/T4/T5 exploratory grids already mined this window for entry/exit shape; reused here for hypothesis-refinement / directional-consistency only, NEVER as a confirmatory read.

fresh.hash_convention: sha256 of json.dumps(sort_keys=True, default=str) of the KEPT signals list only (matches t5_confirmatory_matrix.py's _content_hash -- the file's own embedded sha256/sha256_16 fields use this convention, not a raw-file-bytes hash)
fresh.status: HONEST holdout -- never seen by any exploratory grid before T5. SMALL BY CONSTRUCTION (~13 trading days) -- disclosed, not padded. This is the primary confirmatory read for T-W8.
fresh.reused_from: backtest/tools/t5_confirmatory_matrix.py (build_fresh_slice) -- NOT regenerated; T-W8 verifies+reuses the existing file exactly as T5 left it.

signal_set_integrity.note: Both files are REUSED verbatim from T3/T4/T5 infrastructure per the task's explicit instruction not to reinvent signal generation. T-W8 adds LEVEL CONTEXT (trigger_level / next_opposing_level / headroom_dollars) as a separate enrichment layer computed from SPY bars -- it does not alter or regenerate either signal set.

level_detector.invocation: Per-day FROZEN at the first evaluated bar (time >= 09:35 ET) of each calendar date, replicating lib/orchestrator.py's `_level_per_day` cache exactly (orchestrator.py ~line 917-924: `full_history = spy_df_full[timestamp_et <= bar_time]; _detect_from_history(full_history, bar_date)`, computed once per date and reused for every bar of that session). This is the SAME level set that was ACTIVE in the backtest when lib/filters.py's detect_level_reclaim/detect_level_rejection fired the original BEARISH_REJECTION/BULLISH_RECLAIM triggers -- not a re-derived per-bar snapshot.
level_detector.precedent: Two independent places in this codebase already use this exact per-day-frozen convention for research code built on lib/levels.py: backtest/replay_heartbeat_core.py ports it explicitly (its 'LEVEL-SET PORT' comment states a per-bar re-derivation changes trigger firing vs the orchestrator), and backtest/autoresearch/level_break_first_strike_scan.py computes levels once per day at the first RTH bar independently. T-W8 is not inventing a third convention.
level_detector.c6_look_ahead_guard: frozen_bar_time <= entry_ts for every signal on the same date by construction (the evaluation loop only admits entries at bar_time >= 09:35 ET, so the freeze bar -- itself the first bar >= 09:35 -- is always <= any admitted entry same-day). Verified programmatically by backtest/tests/test_tw8_headroom_retest.py (synthetic future-level leak test).
level_detector.trigger_bar_recovery: entry_spot in the signal set = the TRIGGER bar's close (simulator_real.py, no-look-ahead real-fills path); entry_ts = the FILL/confirmation bar's timestamp, one 5-min bar later (fill.entry_time_et is overwritten to entry_bar_opt.timestamp_et after the initial assignment). The trigger bar is recovered by searching backward from entry_ts on the same date for the bar whose close matches entry_spot within $0.005 (exact-cent match expected; both values originate from the same source CSV). v_pullback_enabled is OFF in the signal-generation params (L2_PATCH never sets it) so this is always the original trigger bar, never a later pullback bar.

H.gate_definition: At signal time, next_opposing_level = the nearest ACTIVE level (from the frozen per-day level set) strictly above entry_spot for calls (bull) / strictly below entry_spot for puts (bear) -- i.e. resistance for calls, support for puts. headroom_dollars = |next_opposing_level - entry_spot|. If no such level exists in the active set, headroom is treated as UNBOUNDED (the gate PASSES -- absence of a detected level is not evidence of nearby structure). Signals with headroom_dollars < threshold are SKIPPED (not replayed, $0, excluded from the kept cohort); headroom_dollars >= threshold (or unbounded) are KEPT and replayed with an UNCHANGED market entry (bars[0] open) -- H only gates ADMISSION, it does not change entry mechanics.
H.eligible_population: every prepared signal in the window (headroom_dollars is computable regardless of whether a literal trigger_level was detected)

R.entry_definition: Instead of a market fill at the recorded confirmation bar, rest a limit AT the trigger_level price (reclaim level for bull / rejection level for bear, both from lib/filters.py's detect_level_reclaim/detect_level_rejection evaluated on the actual trigger bar + the frozen level set -- see level_detector.trigger_bar_recovery). Scan up to `patience` OPTION bars starting at the signal's recorded entry (index 0 = the confirmation bar itself, same indexing convention as t3_entry_matrix.py's entry_fill -- patience counts AVAILABLE option bars, not wall-clock bars, consistent with the existing T3 disclosure about option-bar gaps). At each index i, look up the SPY bar with the SAME timestamp (SPY trades continuously so this lookup essentially never misses) and check the retest condition: filled if spy_bar.low <= trigger_level (calls -- price pulled back down to retest a broken/reclaimed level from above) or spy_bar.high >= trigger_level (puts -- price bounced back up to retest a broken/rejected level from below). On fill at index i, the option ENTRY PREMIUM = that option bar's OPEN (frictionless -- matches the T3/T4/T5 convention of using bar-open fills elsewhere; no penny buffer is applied since this is a chart-structure retest check, not a simulated resting broker limit order on the option premium itself, which IS how T3's own delta-based entry works and does use a penny buffer). Unfilled within `patience` bars = MISSED, priced at $0 and INCLUDED in the denominator -- exactly like T3's cancel-policy convention (a real, counted cost, never excluded).
R.bull_direction_source: explicit in the live hypothesis narrative ("a later bar's low touches the level again")
R.bear_direction_source: symmetric extension by this pre-registration, not explicit in the live hypothesis narrative -- disclosed here rather than silently assumed
R.eligible_population: signals with a detectable trigger_level only (level_context_status starts with 'ok' AND trigger_level is not null). Signals admitted purely via ribbon_flip / sequence_reclaim / confluence-only / trendline / wick triggers -- i.e. no literal level cross on the recovered trigger bar -- have no defined retest anchor and are EXCLUDED from R's cohort, counted and disclosed separately as n_no_level_context (measured: 152/250 exploratory, 4/18 fresh, per the tw8_level_context.py self-check run 2026-07-09).
R.control_comparison_subset: CONTROL exit replayed with a MARKET entry on the SAME eligible population (signals with a trigger_level), for a fair like-for-like delta -- matches t5_confirmatory_matrix.py's cell_metrics 'control_same_eligible_subset' pattern.

candidates.combination_policy: H and R are tested as SEPARATE, independent candidate families against CONTROL (not cross-producted with each other) -- the task frames them as two alternative fixes for the same failure mode, and the fresh-slice n (18) is too small to support a further H x R split without every cell falling below the small-n gate.

CONTROL.label: stop-20/tp+150/sell80/fixed/tgt2.5x/t15:40

exit-A.label: stop-50/tp+150/sell66/trail15/tgt-none/t15:40

exit_shapes.rationale: Both exits so entry-quality x exit-shape interaction is visible (per T3: 'entry offset IS stop headroom' -- a headroom/retest entry fix could interact very differently with a tight -20% stop vs a wide -50% ride, exactly the interaction the T3 entry study found for the passive-limit hypothesis).

fresh.role: HONEST holdout -- the primary confirmatory read, SMALL BY CONSTRUCTION

null_baseline.definition: For each (H threshold, window, exit shape), let k = n_kept under that threshold in that window. Precompute the per-signal replayed pnl for EVERY prepared signal in that window under that exit shape ONCE (market entry, unchanged). Draw N_TRIALS seeded random subsets of size k (without replacement) from the FULL population, average each subset's precomputed pnls, and report the distribution (mean of means, stdev, min, max) across trials. This isolates 'does headroom pick a BETTER-than-random subset of size k' from the trivial fact that dropping any k trades changes the aggregate.
null_baseline.sampling: random.Random(seed).sample(range(n), k) per trial -- deterministic and reproducible given the same population ordering
null_baseline.pass_condition: H's actual kept-cohort expectancy (its own exit shape, its own window) must exceed the null's mean-of-means kept-cohort expectancy (same exit shape, same window) -- otherwise headroom is statistically indistinguishable from randomly dropping the same fraction of trades, i.e. the 'gate' is just trade-count reduction, not a real filter.
null_baseline.applies_to: H only -- R's fill/miss mechanism is not a signal-admission gate over the same population in the same sense (it changes ENTRY PRICE conditional on a retest, not which signals are admitted), so a size-matched random-skip null is not the relevant comparison for R. R's own null is implicit in its pass bar: it must beat CONTROL net of its OWN real misses (priced at $0), which is a stronger, already-adversarial bar (T3 precedent).

pass_bar.definition_source: OP-11 (Karpathy method eval-first gate) applied to this study

components.fresh_slice_delta_vs_control_positive: delta_vs_control_full_population > 0 on the fresh window, for that (candidate, parameter, exit) cell
components.exploratory_delta_vs_control_positive: delta_vs_control_full_population > 0 on the exploratory (BURNED) window, for the SAME cell -- a directional-consistency check, not a confirmatory one, but both must point the same way
components.misses_priced_in: [R only] the miss-as-$0 accounting is a DESIGN INVARIANT verified structurally by the pytest (non-vacuous: n_missed > 0 is asserted to actually occur somewhere in the grid, and expectancy is computed INCLUDING those $0 rows), not a numeric pass/fail threshold
components.skipped_cohort_net_negative: [H only] the skipped cohort's own expectancy (replayed under CONTROL exit) must be <= 0, OR strictly less than the kept cohort's expectancy under the same exit -- evidence the gate removes bad trades, not good ones. Computed per window (small-n permitting)

pass_bar.small_n_handling: a cell with n_eligible (or n_kept, for H) < 8 is marked small_n=true and its component checks are computed for disclosure but the cell verdict is INCONCLUSIVE_SMALL_N, never PASS or FAIL -- matches t5_confirmatory_matrix.py's SMALL_N_THRESHOLD=8 convention exactly, for consistency across the T-series studies.
pass_bar.no_repick_after_fresh_seen: the candidate grid (H thresholds, R patience values, the two exit shapes), the null trial count/seed, and every pass-bar component above are FROZEN in this file before headroom-retest-tw8.json is generated. If every cell fails or is inconclusive, the published verdict is FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE -- that is a valid, publishable outcome per the task directive, not a reason to loosen the bar after the fact.

measured_coverage_at_freeze_time.note: Reference numbers from backtest/tools/tw8_level_context.py's self-check, run 2026-07-09 BEFORE the main study -- included here so a reader can sanity-check n's without re-running. NOT part of the frozen candidate grid itself.

disclosures: qty fixed at 10 (T3/T4/T5 convention) -- absolute $/expectancy is relative-to-control, not an OP-16 account-scaled number.
Frictionless fills at trigger/retest levels; 5-min OPRA bars (touch semantics; 1-min close timing not modelled, same disclosed gap as T3/T4/T5).
Premium-only replay: ribbon-flip / level / chart exits OFF (same convention as every prior T-series study) -- only the two named exit shapes are tested.
ribbon_ride only (both directions) -- vwap_continuation is a separate setup path, not in scope (ground rule 11, carried from T3/T4/T5).
No real-fills anchor (layer b) in this study -- T-W8 is exploratory+fresh-slice only. An anchor is owed separately if any candidate here reaches a confirmatory PASS.

Fresh window n=18 is SMALL BY CONSTRUCTION; per-direction/per-threshold/per-patience cells will frequently fall below the small_n_threshold=8 gate -- expected and disclosed, not padded or re-windowed.

R's retest scan aligns OPTION bars to SPY bars by exact timestamp match; SPY trades continuously so this lookup is not expected to miss, but any miss is counted as n_spy_bar_lookup_miss and disclosed rather than silently treated as a fill or a skip.

trigger_level coverage is a real constraint on R's eligible population (measured 98/250 exploratory, 14/18 fresh) -- the majority of ribbon_ride signals are admitted via ribbon_flip/sequence/confluence-only triggers without a literal level cross on the recovered trigger bar, and those signals cannot be given a retest anchor.

H's headroom is computed from lib/levels.py's approximation of chart structure (5-day rolling H/L, POC, anchored VWAP, round numbers, etc. -- see levels.py's own docstring) -- it is NOT the live level_memory.py shadow multi-day feed (wired live 2026-07-09, same day as this hypothesis) since level_memory has no historical backtest presence over either window; this study answers 'would the BACKTEST's own level definition have flagged this' not 'would the live memory feed have flagged this'.
